subject.title: fix(codex): stop stale MCP child processes with revalidated SIGKILL escalation

question: Should the macOS Codex Computer Use health monitor guarantee forced SIGKILL of a stale helper that survives two seconds, rather than retaining the existing best-effort SIGTERM-only lifecycle?
rationale: The code can implement either lifecycle, but the acceptable shutdown deadline and consequences for a real bundled helper are an owner-level behavior contract that Linux-only proof cannot settle.

options.title: Approve bounded escalation after Darwin proof
options.body: Keep the two-second SIGKILL escalation if a redacted macOS app-server run proves the stale helper is terminated and normal helper behavior remains safe.

options.title: Keep SIGTERM-only cleanup
options.body: Reject forced termination if the bundled helper requires a longer or owner-managed shutdown lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded escalation after Darwin proof
recommendation.body: Keep the two-second SIGKILL escalation if a redacted macOS app-server run proves the stale helper is terminated and normal helper behavior remains safe.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner must define the intended shutdown semantics for the bundled helper path.
